Definition: middle voice from the same as G2436; to conciliate, i.e. (transitively) to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious:--be merciful, make reconciliation for.
BiblicalUsage: hiláskomai means be merciful, make reconciliation for. It turns up twice, in Luke and Hebrews.
TheologicalSignificance: I take hiláskomai as it stands — be merciful, make reconciliation for — and read the passage with that plain sense in mind.
RelatedEvents: The Pharisee and the Tax Collector
